data.narrative:
GITAI, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Sho Nakanose, has raised $129M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—including Hadrian, Agile Robots, Nimble Robotics, Divergent, and Exotec at similar stages.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $129M total raised as a baseline and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, implying a valuation of $219M. The peer-median method examines three same-sector, same-stage companies: Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B). The median of this cohort is $1.0B, with a range of $1.0B–$1.6B.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $186M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $610M. The wide dispersion reflects meaningful uncertainty around GITAI's competitive positioning relative to better-capitalized peers. The stage-progression method suggests GITAI trades below median peer valuations, while the peer-median approach anchors to observable market comparables. Key uncertainties include customer concentration, technology differentiation relative to Hadrian and Agile Robots, and the trajectory of Series C robotics funding multiples. A fair-value estimate would center toward the $610M median, with upside contingent on demonstrated commercial traction.
